model.rationale: The district's 21-point Democratic lean, Khanna's incumbency, and a fundraising gap of $13.7 million raised versus under $38,000 leave Tandon without a visible path. Markets price Khanna near certain, and the lopsided money picture justifies expecting a margin even wider than the district lean alone implies.
model.watch: With no polling in the race, only a late scandal or a sudden wave of outside spending against Khanna would be a visible signal, and even that would face a steep district lean.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 17th District sits in the heart of Silicon Valley and leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 21 points. Ro Khanna, the incumbent, advanced to the general election and carries the full weight of incumbency in a seat his party comfortably holds. His campaign has raised more than $13.7 million and holds roughly $16.9 million on hand, while Republican challenger Ritesh Tandon has raised under $38,000 and reports less than $1,000 available.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Khanna's chances near 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money gap leaves little room for an upset, so the seat is rated Safe Democratic with Khanna favored to win by a wide margin. The main uncertainty is the size of the victory, since no polling exists to anchor expectations.
